package: TrackShift / OVERTIQ energy and overtake model
scope: 2026 Formula 1 season, 13 races with complete feeds. 2025 data deliberately excluded: different power unit regulations, no Overtake mode.

provenance_legend.MEASURED: present in the source feed as recorded by the timing/telemetry supplier
provenance_legend.DERIVED: computed by us from MEASURED data by a documented formula
provenance_legend.ESTIMATED: output of a model with free parameters calibrated against data
provenance_legend.ASSUMED: a constant we chose; no data supports the specific value
provenance_legend.REGULATORY: read from the FIA 2026 Formula 1 Technical Regulations

sources.note: car_data is ~4 Hz per driver. The 2026 sessions carry NO ERS, SOC, deployment or DRS content: the drs field is empty on every 2026 session.

articles_used.C5.2.8: non-Overtake and Overtake ERS-K power curves vs speed
articles_used.C4.1/C4.7: minimum mass and nominal tyre mass

sources.note: built from the OpenF1 location feed (x, y, z at ~4 Hz) by fitting a centreline and arc length; gives track_s, curvature, gradient, offset.
CdA and rolling terms fitted per session from coast-down segments of the measured telemetry; see params/vehicle_identification.json for per-session CI.

telemetry.resolution: source cadence, nominally 4 Hz; the per-session median sample interval is reported below. It is NOT a uniform 0.25 s grid: intervals vary and gaps occur.

files.cda_note: session CdA 0.49 not credible; calendar median 1.0 used
session CdA None not credible; calendar median 1.0 used

t: seconds since the session feed start, the join key with the source
dt: seconds since this driver's previous sample; NaN if > 1 s (not integrated)
lap_ok: sample lies inside that lap's recorded duration + 2 s
neutral: inside a safety car / VSC / red flag window (race_control), padded 10 s before and 30 s after
overtake_legal: outside an OVERTAKE DISABLED window in the race_control feed
a_smoothed_ms2: longitudinal acceleration, centred rolling mean over ~1 s of the source-derived value
grade_sin: sine of the longitudinal gradient, differenced from this car's own z along its own path. NULL on stationary and pit-lane samples (0 % null among moving samples, v > 54 km/h). This is the channel the power split uses.
curv: signed curvature, 1/m, differenced from this car's own path. Same null pattern as grade_sin.
grade_here: gradient interpolated from the fitted track map at this arc length. Never null. Correlates 0.990 with grade_sin on moving samples and gives an identical grade-power distribution (mean |P| 12.0 vs 11.8 kW at Spa); use it if you want a gap-free channel.
curv_here: curvature from the fitted track map at this arc length. Never null.
track_s: arc length from the start line, m
track_offset_m: lateral offset from the fitted centreline, m
dist_to_next_corner_m: metres to the next curvature peak
p_rolling_kw: c_roll * m * v / 1000, c_roll ASSUMED 0.30 m/s^2
p_wheel_kw: sum of the four terms above: total power at the wheels
drag_tow_factor: drag multiplier for running in a tow: 0.80 inside 0.5 s, 0.86 at 0.5-1.0 s, 1.0 otherwise
fuel_flow_limit_kw: C5.2.4 min(3000, 0.27*rpm + 165) MJ/h expressed in kW
p_ice_kw: eta_ice * fuel_flow_limit_kw * throttle/100; eta_ice calibrated per race so the median green lap closes
p_ers_demand_kw: p_wheel_kw / eta_drive - p_ice_kw; positive means the battery is being drawn on
ers_curve_limit_kw: C5.2.8 Overtake or non-Overtake ERS-K ceiling at this speed, per the race_control state
p_deploy_kw: clip(p_ers_demand_kw, 0, ers_curve_limit_kw), zero at closed throttle
p_regen_kw: min(rear_share * |p_wheel_kw|, 350 kW) * eta_regen while braking; rear_share ASSUMED 0.40
soc_mj: running integral clip(SOC - (deploy - regen) dt, 0, 4 MJ). The LEVEL is set by the clipping, not observed. Use the within-lap shape and per-lap totals, not the absolute value.
zone_id: index of the >290 kph zone this sample is inside, -1 if none
dist_to_zone_m: metres to the entry of the next >290 kph zone, 0 inside one
gap_ahead: seconds to the car ahead, latest intervals reading, accepted up to 15 s stale. Source cadence is ~4 s. Null on ~44 % of all samples but only ~15 % of in-lap (lap_ok) samples: the remainder are pit, grid, formation and out-lap samples, plus the race leader, who has no car ahead.
gap_closing_rate_s_per_s: d(gap)/dt of the smoothed intervals series. COARSE: inherits the ~4 s source cadence.
approach_speed_kph_equiv: -gap_closing_rate * v_kph: an equivalent closing speed. Same coarseness caveat.
cda_m2: session drag area from the coast-down fit
mass_kg: 724 kg regulatory + 44 kg nominal tyres + 35 kg session-mean fuel = 803 kg
eta_ice_calibrated: the single free scalar of the energy balance, one value per race

null_patterns.grade_sin / curv: null on stationary and pit-lane samples only; 0 % null among moving samples. grade_here / curv_here are the never-null track-map equivalents.
null_patterns.gap_ahead and its derivatives: ~15 % null among in-lap samples (leader, or no intervals reading within 15 s); ~44 % across all samples including pit and formation laps.
null_patterns.dt: null where the gap to the previous sample exceeded 1 s; those samples are excluded from every energy integral.
null_patterns.lap / lap_ok: lap_ok is False outside a recorded lap window; the analysis sets always filter on it.

not_available.true_SOC: no public feed carries it. soc_mj is our estimate.
not_available.MGU-K measured power / torque / efficien: not published. Only the regulatory ceiling curves are known; eta_drive 0.95 and eta_regen 0.90 are ASSUMED.
not_available.battery capacity, voltage, internal resi: not published. Only the 4 MJ regulatory swing is used.
not_available.ICE torque curve: not published. We model ICE power as a fraction of the regulatory fuel-flow limit scaled by throttle; there is no torque map.
not_available.DRS: the drs field is empty for every 2026 session.

zone_events.parquet.grain: one passage of one >290 kph zone by one car
outcome: passed: this car passed the car that was ahead at zone entry, between zone entry and zone exit + 8 s, per the overtakes feed

gap_entry: gap to the car ahead at zone entry, s
leader: car number that was ahead at zone entry, from the position feed
rival_deployed: the leader's own deployment at the same zone and lap
prev_zone_own_deployed / prev_zone_rival: what each car did at the previous zone of the same lap
own_deploys_earlier_in_lap / rival_deplo: cumulative deployments earlier in this lap
vmax: top speed inside the zone, km/h
neutral / lap_ok / legal: cleanliness flags; the analysis set is ~neutral & lap_ok & leader>0 & gap_entry<=2.5

zone_events.parquet.exclusions: safety car / VSC / red flag windows, samples outside a recorded lap

lap_trials.parquet.grain: one 60 s non-overlapping trial for one follower-leader pair
outcome: passed (60 s), lost_place, durable3 (passed and still ahead 3 laps later), gained3 (race position improved)
lap_trials.parquet.exclusions: first 180 s of the race, neutralised windows padded 10/30 s, pit windows +/-90 s for either car, gaps over 5 s
lap_trials.parquet.note: clean3 marks trials with a usable +3-lap window (neither car pitted, no neutralisation started, race not over): 86 % qualify

params.constants.json: every regulatory, assumed and measured constant used anywhere in the pipeline
params.vehicle_identification.json: per-session CdA with 95 % CI, air density, assumed mass, coast-fit diagnostics
params.zones_by_circuit.json: the >290 km/h zones per circuit: start and end arc length, length. Derived from the field's median speed profile in 10 m bins.

zone_pass_model.name: P(pass in this zone passage)
zone_pass_model.target: passed: this car passed the car that was ahead at zone entry, between zone entry and zone exit + 8 s (overtakes feed)

feature_definitions.gap: gap_entry, seconds to the car ahead at zone entry (intervals feed, latest reading)
feature_definitions.tyre_delta: own tyre age minus the car ahead's, laps (stints feed); NaN -> 0
feature_definitions.own_dep: 1 if this car drew >= 0.12 MJ inside the zone (ESTIMATED), else 0
feature_definitions.rival_dep: same for the car ahead, same zone same lap (ESTIMATED); NaN -> 0
feature_definitions.next_km: metres from this zone's exit to the next zone's entry, /1000, capped 6
feature_definitions.is_last: 1 if this is the final zone of the lap

zone_pass_model.preprocessing: none: raw units, no scaler, no encoder. NaN handling as stated per feature.
zone_pass_model.output: probability in [0,1] via 1/(1+exp(-x.b)), x prefixed with a 1.0 intercept column

rival_cover_model.name: P(the car ahead deploys in this zone)
rival_cover_model.target: rival_dep: the car ahead drew >= 0.12 MJ in this zone (ESTIMATED)

feature_definitions.rival_soc: car ahead's ESTIMATED SOC at zone entry, MJ; NaN -> 2.5
feature_definitions.rival_deploys_earlier: count of zones this lap where the car ahead already deployed
feature_definitions.rival_prev_zone: 1 if the car ahead deployed at the previous zone of this lap; NaN -> 0.5
feature_definitions.rival_gap_ahead_of_them: the car ahead's own gap to the car in front of it, s, capped 5; NaN -> 5
feature_definitions.gap: our gap to them at zone entry, s
feature_definitions.tyre_delta: our tyre age minus theirs, laps
feature_definitions.zone_idx: index of the zone within the lap, 0-based

rival_cover_model.preprocessing: none: raw units, NaN fills as stated
rival_cover_model.output: probability the car ahead covers; used as c in the policy EV

deployment_policy.name: per-zone deploy decision
deployment_policy.tau_units: probability of a pass, per deployment
deployment_policy.note: uses no information dated after the decision instant

lap_trial_models.note: 60 s trial horizon, superseded by the zone models for deployment decisions but used for the attack/hold/defend call

pass_60s.target: a pass of the car ahead within 60 s (overtakes feed)

durable_pass_3laps.target: passed within 60 s AND still ahead of that car 3 laps later, clean window only

mlp.warning: IN-SAMPLE fit for interface completeness. The LOCO evaluation (reports/haas_eval/gpu_pass_model.json) showed the MLP does not beat the logistic out of fold; the logistic is the shipped model.

models.how_to_score: p = 1/(1+exp(-(b0 + sum(b_i * x_i)))) with the features in feature_order, raw units, no scaling. The MLP is the only artefact needing the bundled scaler.

descriptions.zone_measure.json: raw per-zone measurement: pass rate by gap at entry crossed with who deployed; the sequencing tables; per-zone base rates
descriptions.zone_policy.json: the LOCO zone pass model, the 2x2 Nash solution per zone, within-lap sequencing by backward induction, and a first backtest
descriptions.zone_realtime.json: the rival-coverage model and the honest real-time policy backtest, including the perfect-information oracle
descriptions.haas_eval.json: lap-level Haas evaluation: outcome metrics, feature information, probability quality, Q2 metrics, defending
descriptions.gpu_pass_model.json: MLP leave-one-circuit-out check and drop-one ablations against the logistic
descriptions.soc_calibration.json: per-race eta_ice, lap closure spread, parameter sensitivity, and the two estimator validations

known_limitations: No measured energy channel exists. Every SOC, deployment and harvesting number is an estimate from an energy balance with one calibrated scalar and several assumed constants. Per-lap totals carry about +/-25 % from the assumed 0.40 regen share alone.
The SOC level is pinned by clipping at 0 and 4 MJ (15-27 % of laps touch the floor, 27-39 % the ceiling). Use the shape and the per-lap totals, not the absolute level.
The drag model books slipstream as deployment unless the tow correction is applied. These files use the tow-corrected (strong) variant; the correction factor itself is ASSUMED, not fitted.
Gap data comes from the intervals feed at roughly 4 s cadence. Closing rates derived from it are correspondingly coarse.
13 races is 11 circuits with zones (Monaco and the Hungaroring have none above 290 km/h). Bootstrap confidence intervals on precision are about +/-0.05.
Monaco has telemetry for only 7 % of its trials. Shanghai's fitted CdA (0.49) was not credible and the calendar median was substituted.
Zone passes are 624 of 2,916 total passes: roughly one pass in five happens in an Overtake zone. The zone model addresses that fifth.
The 'expected extra passes' in the backtests are the model's own causal estimate summed over a policy's deploy set, not counted outcomes. They are only as good as the model's deployment coefficient.
